# Expanded Text

The paper investigates the structural theory of strongly self-absorbing C*-algebras, focusing on the classification of unital *-homomorphisms into stabilized algebras and the topological properties of automorphism groups arising from such algebras. Let us elaborate on each of the main results.

## Main Setting and the Upgrade from Approximate to Asymptotic Unitary Equivalence

The paper begins with a foundational setup: let $D$ be a unital, separable, strongly self-absorbing C*-algebra, and let $A$ be a unital, separable C*-algebra. It is a well-established fact in the classification program for C*-algebras that unital *-homomorphisms from $D$ into $A \otimes D$ satisfying certain natural conditions (typically arising from the same $KK$-class or satisfying suitable approximate intertwining properties) are approximately unitarily equivalent. This means that for any two such homomorphisms $\varphi, \psi : D \to A \otimes D$, one can find a sequence of unitaries $(u_n)$ in $A \otimes D$ such that $u_n \varphi(d) u_n^* \to \psi(d)$ for all $d \in D$, but the convergence is only assured "in the limit" over a sequence, without any control on the path connecting the unitaries.

The central technical contribution of the paper is to show that when $D$ is additionally assumed to be **$K_1$-injective** (meaning that the map $U(D)/U_0(D) \to K_1(D)$ is injective, a mild and widely satisfied hypothesis for known strongly self-absorbing algebras), this approximate equivalence can be substantially strengthened to **asymptotic unitary equivalence**. This means that there exists a continuous path of unitaries $(u_t)_{t \in [0,\infty)}$ in $A \otimes D$ such that
$$
\lim_{t \to \infty} \| u_t \varphi(d) u_t^* - \psi(d) \| = 0 \quad \text{for all } d \in D.
$$
This is a considerably stronger and more rigid form of equivalence, as it requires the unitaries to vary continuously in $t$, rather than merely admitting a discrete sequence achieving the limit. The upgrade from approximate to asymptotic unitary equivalence is technically delicate and constitutes the main analytical achievement of the paper, relying on careful control of paths in unitary groups and exploiting the self-absorbing structure of $D$ together with $K_1$-injectivity to remove topological obstructions in $K_1(D)$.

## Consequence: Endomorphisms of $D$ are Asymptotically Inner

As a direct and conceptually important consequence of this asymptotic uniqueness theorem, the authors deduce that **every unital endomorphism of $D$ is asymptotically inner**. That is, for any unital *-homomorphism $\phi : D \to D$, there exists a continuous path of unitaries $(u_t)$ in $D$ such that $u_t \phi(d) u_t^* \to d$ as $t \to \infty$, for every $d \in D$. This result reflects the extremely rigid internal structure of strongly self-absorbing algebras: essentially, up to asymptotic conjugation, there is only one unital endomorphism of $D$, namely the identity. This significantly refines earlier results, which typically established only that endomorphisms are approximately inner (in the sequential, non-continuous sense), by now guaranteeing a genuinely continuous asymptotic path.

## Compact-Contractibility of the Automorphism Group

Building on the asymptotic innerness of endomorphisms, the paper proceeds to study the topological structure of the group $\mathrm{Aut}(D)$ of automorphisms of $D$, equipped with the **point-norm topology** (i.e., the topology of pointwise convergence in norm). The authors show that this space is **compactly-contractible**: for every compact Hausdorff space $X$, the set of homotopy classes of continuous maps $[X, \mathrm{Aut}(D)]$ collapses to a single point. In other words, any continuous map from a compact Hausdorff space into $\mathrm{Aut}(D)$ is homotopic to a constant map, and moreover this holds uniformly with respect to arbitrary compact parameter spaces $X$, not merely for $X$ a point or an interval. This is a strong topological triviality statement, generalizing ordinary contractibility (which corresponds to the case $X = $ a point or an interval) to the much broader class of all compact Hausdorff spaces. An entirely analogous compact-contractibility statement is established for the (typically non-invertible) unital endomorphisms of $D$, extending the automorphism result to this larger monoid of self-maps.

This compact-contractibility phenomenon reflects, at the level of mapping spaces, the same rigidity captured by the K₁-injectivity and asymptotic uniqueness results: not only is every automorphism asymptotically inner, but families of automorphisms parametrized continuously over compact spaces can be contracted to the identity in a manner compatible with the topology of the parameter space.

## Application: A Description of $KK(D, A \otimes D)$

As a significant application of these structural results, the authors provide an explicit description of the **Kasparov $K$-theory group** $KK(D, A \otimes D)$ purely in terms of *-homomorphisms and asymptotic unitary equivalence. Specifically, they show that $KK(D, A \otimes D)$ can be realized as the set of asymptotic unitary equivalence classes of unital *-homomorphisms from $D$ to $A \otimes D$ (suitably interpreted to account for the semigroup/group structure via stabilization). This provides a very concrete and geometrically meaningful model for the Kasparov group in this setting, bypassing the usual technical machinery of Kasparov modules and instead expressing $KK$-theory directly via honest *-homomorphisms up to a natural and computable equivalence relation.

## Isomorphism with $K_0(A \otimes D)$

Finally, en route to this application, the authors establish the auxiliary but important result that
$$
KK(D, A \otimes D) \cong K_0(A \otimes D).
$$
This isomorphism identifies the Kasparov group of maps from $D$ into $A \otimes D$ with the ordinary $K_0$-group of the stabilized algebra $A \otimes D$, reflecting the fact that, due to the strong self-absorption of $D$, the $KK$-theoretic information carried by $D$ as the domain becomes essentially equivalent to ordinary $K$-theoretic data on the target algebra. This isomorphism plays a crucial technical role in the proof of the main application described above, as it allows the authors to translate between the abstract $KK$-theoretic framework and the concrete classification of *-homomorphisms up to asymptotic unitary equivalence.

# Unital *-Homomorphisms into $A \otimes \mathcal{D}$ for Strongly Self-Absorbing $\mathcal{D}$

## Introduction

Strongly self-absorbing C*-algebras occupy a central position in the classification program for nuclear C*-algebras, serving both as fundamental building blocks and as regularity witnesses for a wide class of C*-algebras. Recall that a separable unital C*-algebra $\mathcal{D}$ is *strongly self-absorbing* if $\mathcal{D} \neq \mathbb{C}$ and there exists an isomorphism $\varphi: \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{D} \otimes \mathcal{D}$ that is approximately unitarily equivalent to the map $d \mapsto d \otimes 1_{\mathcal{D}}$. Examples include the Cuntz algebras $\mathcal{O}_2$ and $\mathcal{O}_\infty$, the UHF algebras of infinite type, and their tensor products with $\mathcal{O}_\infty$. The self-absorption property, encoded in the McDuff-type condition above, forces remarkably rigid behavior for morphisms taking values in $\mathcal{D}$-stable algebras.

A cornerstone result in this theory, due to Kirchberg and Winter, and further developed by Toms–Winter, Dadarlat–Winter, and others, asserts that for a $K_1$-injective strongly self-absorbing C*-algebra $\mathcal{D}$, any two unital *-homomorphisms $\varphi, \psi: \mathcal{D} \to A \otimes \mathcal{D}$ that agree on the level of the associated $KK$-classes are *approximately unitarily equivalent*: there exists a sequence (or net) of unitaries $u_n \in \mathcal{U}(A \otimes \mathcal{D})$ such that $u_n \varphi(d) u_n^* \to \psi(d)$ for all $d \in \mathcal{D}$. Here $K_1$-injectivity refers to the condition that the natural map $K_1(\mathcal{D}) \to K_1(\mathcal{D} \otimes \mathcal{D})$ (equivalently, the map from unitaries in $\mathcal{D}$ modulo the connected component of the identity into the corresponding group for $\mathcal{D} \otimes \mathcal{D}$) is injective; this technical hypothesis is known to be automatically satisfied for a large class of examples and is conjectured to hold universally among strongly self-absorbing algebras.

The purpose of this paper is to sharpen this approximate statement to an *asymptotic* one. We show that under the same hypotheses—$\mathcal{D}$ strongly self-absorbing and $K_1$-injective—unitarily equivalent unital embeddings $\varphi, \psi: \mathcal{D} \to A \otimes \mathcal{D}$ are in fact *asymptotically* unitarily equivalent: there exists a continuous path of unitaries $(u_t)_{t \in [0,\infty)}$ in $A \otimes \mathcal{D}$, with $u_0 = 1$, such that
$$
\lim_{t \to \infty} \| u_t \varphi(d) u_t^* - \psi(d) \| = 0 \qquad \text{for all } d \in \mathcal{D}.
$$
This upgrade from a discrete sequence of approximating unitaries to a continuous asymptotic path is not merely a cosmetic strengthening. It reflects a deeper homotopical rigidity phenomenon: the space of unital embeddings of $\mathcal{D}$ into $A \otimes \mathcal{D}$, up to unitary equivalence, behaves as though it were governed by a genuinely continuous homotopy theory, rather than merely an approximation-theoretic one. The technical heart of the proof involves an intertwining argument combined with a careful analysis of paths of unitaries implementing the approximate equivalences at each stage, glued together using a reparametrization and stabilization technique adapted to the self-absorption structure of $\mathcal{D}$.

This asymptotic uniqueness theorem has several structural consequences of independent interest, which we develop in the sequel.

**Endomorphisms are asymptotically inner.** Applying the main theorem to the case $A = \mathbb{C}$, we deduce that every unital endomorphism $\varphi: \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{D}$ is asymptotically inner: there is a continuous path of unitaries $u_t \in \mathcal{D}$ with $u_t \varphi(d) u_t^* \to d$ for every $d \in \mathcal{D}$. This recovers and extends earlier approximate innerness results and shows that, up to asymptotic unitary equivalence, the identity representation of $\mathcal{D}$ is the unique unital embedding of $\mathcal{D}$ into itself compatible with the trivial $KK$-class.

**Compact contractibility of the automorphism group.** A further consequence concerns the topological structure of $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{D})$, the automorphism group of $\mathcal{D}$ equipped with the point-norm topology. We show that this space is *compactly contractible*: every compact subset of $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{D})$ can be contracted, within a (possibly larger) compact set, to the identity automorphism through a continuous homotopy of automorphisms. This strengthens the previously known contractibility (in the weaker, approximate sense) of the automorphism space, and provides a genuine continuous null-homotopy at the level of compact families of automorphisms, a fact with implications for the classification of actions of $\mathcal{D}$ on itself and for the computation of related homotopy and cohomology theories associated with $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{D})$.

**A description of $KK(\mathcal{D}, A \otimes \mathcal{D})$.** Finally, combining the asymptotic uniqueness theorem with existence results for unital embeddings realizing prescribed $KK$-classes, we obtain a concrete geometric model for the Kasparov group $KK(\mathcal{D}, A \otimes \mathcal{D})$: every class is represented by a unital *-homomorphism $\mathcal{D} \to A \otimes \mathcal{D}$, and two such homomorphisms represent the same class if and only if they are asymptotically unitarily equivalent. In particular, this identifies $KK(\mathcal{D}, A\otimes \mathcal{D})$ with the set of asymptotic unitary equivalence classes of unital embeddings of $\mathcal{D}$ into $A \otimes \mathcal{D}$. Coupled with the known computation identifying $KK(\mathcal{D}, A \otimes \mathcal{D})$ with $K_0(A \otimes \mathcal{D})$ via evaluation against the class of $\mathcal{D}$ itself (using the self-absorption of $\mathcal{D}$ and standard Künneth-type arguments), we arrive at a natural isomorphism
$$
KK(\mathcal{D}, A \otimes \mathcal{D}) \; \cong \; K_0(A \otimes \mathcal{D}),
$$
realized entirely in terms of asymptotic unitary equivalence classes of unital *-homomorphisms. This provides a purely $C^*$-algebraic, homotopy-theoretic avatar of the $K$-theoretic isomorphism, and situates the classification of embeddings of $\mathcal{D}$ inside $A\otimes\mathcal{D}$ within the same framework used for the classification of $\mathcal{D}$-stable C*-algebras more broadly.

The remainder of the paper is organized as follows. In Section 2 we recall the necessary preliminaries on strongly self-absorbing algebras, $K_1$-injectivity, and the approximate uniqueness theorem that serves as our starting point. Section 3 contains the proof of the asymptotic uniqueness theorem, via an inductive construction of a continuously varying family of unitaries. Section 4 derives the consequence that endomorphisms of $\mathcal{D}$ are asymptotically inner and establishes the compact contractibility of $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{D})$. Section 5 develops the identification of $KK(\mathcal{D}, A \otimes \mathcal{D})$ with the set of asymptotic unitary equivalence classes of unital embeddings, and concludes with the isomorphism to $K_0(A \otimes \mathcal{D})$.

# The Importance of Continuous Learning

In today's rapidly evolving world, the ability to learn continuously has become more valuable than ever before. Technology changes, industries transform, and the skills that were once considered essential can quickly become obsolete. Adapting to this reality requires a mindset shift—one that embraces learning not as a finite phase of life, but as an ongoing journey.

Let us consider how this applies to the modern workplace. Professionals today are expected to master new tools, understand emerging trends, and remain flexible in the face of constant change. Employees who commit to lifelong learning are often better equipped to navigate uncertainty, solve complex problems, and contribute meaningfully to their organizations. Whether through formal education, online courses, or self-directed exploration, the opportunities to grow one's knowledge base are virtually limitless.

This growth mindset extends beyond professional development—it enriches personal lives as well. Learning a new language, picking up a musical instrument, or exploring a scientific concept purely out of curiosity can bring immense satisfaction and open new perspectives. This kind of intellectual engagement keeps the mind sharp and fosters a sense of purpose that many find deeply fulfilling.

Moreover, continuous learning strengthens resilience. When individuals cultivate the habit of acquiring new skills and knowledge, they become more adaptable to unexpected challenges—whether these arise from economic shifts, technological disruptions, or personal circumstances. Moreover, this adaptability often translates into greater confidence, as learners realize that they possess the capacity to tackle unfamiliar situations effectively.

Ultimately, embracing lifelong learning is not just a strategy for career advancement; it is a philosophy for living a richer, more engaged life. By remaining curious and open to new ideas, individuals position themselves to thrive amid change, seize emerging opportunities, and contribute positively to the world around them.

# On Asymptotic Unitary Equivalence of Embeddings into Strongly Self-Absorbing Tensor Products

## Abstract

Let $D$ be a unital separable strongly self-absorbing $C^*$-algebra which is $K_1$-injective, and let $A$ be a unital separable $C^*$-algebra. We study the classification of unital $*$-homomorphisms $D \to A \otimes D$ up to approximate/asymptotic unitary equivalence, extending the Dadarlat–Winter framework beyond the classical $KK$-obstruction theory.

Our first main structural result establishes that the semigroups $\mathrm{Aut}(D)$ and $\mathrm{End}(D)$, equipped with the point-norm topology, are **contractible**. This is achieved by exploiting the self-absorption property $D \cong D \otimes D^{\otimes \infty}$ together with a Kirchberg-type approximate intertwining argument to construct explicit contractions through asymptotic morphisms compatible with the strongly self-absorbing tensorial structure. The contractibility of $\mathrm{Aut}(D)$ in particular yields vanishing of the higher homotopy groups $\pi_n(\mathrm{Aut}(D)) = 0$ for all $n \geq 0$, a fact essential for the rigidity results below.

Building on this, we prove:

**Theorem A.** Let $\phi, \psi : D \to A \otimes D$ be unital $*$-homomorphisms. Then $\phi$ and $\psi$ are asymptotically unitarily equivalent if and only if they induce the same class in $KK(D, A \otimes D)$.

The proof proceeds via a two-sided intertwining argument: contractibility of $\mathrm{Aut}(D)$ furnishes continuous paths of automorphisms absorbing perturbations arising from Elliott-type approximate unitary equivalences at each stage of an inductive limit decomposition, while $K_1$-injectivity of $D$ ensures that unitaries in $A \otimes D$ implementing the $KK$-equivalence can be lifted to genuine asymptotic unitary paths, circumventing potential $K_1(D)$-obstructions.

As a structural consequence, using the self-absorption $D \otimes D \cong D$, we establish:

**Theorem B.** There is a natural bijection
$$
KK(D, A \otimes D) \;\cong\; K_0(A \otimes D),
$$
compatible with the semigroup structure induced by Kasparov product, identifying the class of a unital embedding $D \hookrightarrow A \otimes D$ with the class $[1_A \otimes 1_D] \in K_0(A \otimes D)$ under the canonical splitting.

Together, Theorems A and B show that unital embeddings $D \to A \otimes D$ are classified, up to asymptotic unitary equivalence, entirely by $K$-theoretic data: the map
$$
[\phi] \mapsto [\phi]_{K_0} \in K_0(A \otimes D)
$$
is a complete asymptotic unitary equivalence invariant. This subsumes known results for $D = \mathcal{O}_\infty, \mathcal{O}_2, \mathcal{Z}$, and UHF algebras of infinite type, and provides the technical foundation for classification of unital embeddings and, via a standard two-sided intertwining argument, for the classification of $D$-absorbing extensions and $D$-stable $C^*$-dynamical systems up to cocycle conjugacy.

# Asymptotic Unitary Equivalence and K1-Injectivity of Strongly Self-Absorbing C*-Algebras

## Abstract

We investigate the structural consequences of K1-injectivity for strongly self-absorbing (s.s.a.) C*-algebras, establishing that this K-theoretic hypothesis upgrades the well-known approximate unitary equivalence of unital \*-homomorphisms into a stronger, asymptotic form of unitary equivalence. Let $D$ be a strongly self-absorbing C*-algebra satisfying the K1-injectivity condition, meaning the canonical map $K_1(D) \to K_1(D)^{as}$ (or equivalently, the unitary group condition relating $U(D)$ to its image in the corona/asymptotic algebra) is injective. Our central technical result shows that any two unital \*-homomorphisms $\varphi, \psi: D \to D \otimes \mathcal{K} \otimes \mathbb{C}$ or more generally into a suitable stabilization, which are approximately unitarily equivalent, are in fact *asymptotically* unitarily equivalent: there exists a continuous path of unitaries $(u_t)_{t \in [0,\infty)}$ such that $\mathrm{Ad}(u_t) \circ \varphi \to \psi$ pointwise in norm as $t \to \infty$, with the path implementing the equivalence continuously rather than merely through a sequence.

Building on this rigidity phenomenon, we derive several structural consequences. First, we show that under K1-injectivity, every unital endomorphism of $D$ that is approximately inner is automatically asymptotically inner, and consequently the space of unital endomorphisms of $D$ approximately equivalent to the identity is *contractible* when equipped with the point-norm topology; the asymptotic unitary path furnishes an explicit contraction. This addresses a question originating in the work of Effros-Rosenberg and connects to Dadarlat-Eilers-type classification programs. Second, we characterize the group of connected components of unital endomorphisms of $D$ via $K$-theory: we prove that $\pi_0(\mathrm{End}^1(D)) \cong K_0(D)$, with the isomorphism realized through the index map associated to asymptotic unitary equivalence classes, generalizing prior computations for $\mathcal{O}_\infty$-absorbing and UHF-type algebras. Third, we establish a $KK$-theoretic rigidity statement: two unital \*-homomorphisms $D \to D$ inducing the same class in $KK(D,D)$ are asymptotically unitarily equivalent whenever $D$ is K1-injective, thereby showing that $KK$-equivalence classes of unital endomorphisms coincide precisely with asymptotic unitary equivalence classes, and that the semigroup structure on $[D,D]$ is governed entirely by $K_0(D)$ as a ring.

These results substantially extend the classification theory of endomorphisms of strongly self-absorbing algebras beyond the previously known cases (such as the Cuntz algebra $\mathcal{O}_2$, where K1-injectivity trivially holds due to $K_*(\mathcal{O}_2) = 0$), to encompass UHF algebras, $\mathcal{O}_\infty$, the Jiang-Su algebra $\mathcal{Z}$, and tensor products thereof, provided K1-injectivity is verified or assumed. We further discuss the relationship between K1-injectivity and the Rosenberg-type conjecture asserting this property holds for all strongly self-absorbing C*-algebras, and indicate how our asymptotic equivalence theorem would resolve, in full generality, questions about the topological triviality of the space of approximately inner automorphisms and endomorphisms of $D$, with applications to the classification of *-automorphisms of $D \otimes \mathcal{K}$ up to asymptotic unitary equivalence and to the computation of the K-theory of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(D)$ as a topological group.

**Keywords:** strongly self-absorbing C*-algebras, K1-injectivity, asymptotic unitary equivalence, KK-theory, endomorphism semigroups, Jiang-Su algebra, classification theory
